tools.name: list_services
tools.description: Every document Claim Done drafts, with its live flat price in AUD, what the person receives and how it is delivered.

tools.name: match_problem
tools.description: Takes a plain-English description of the person's problem (who, what happened, what they want) and returns the Claim Done document that fits, its price in AUD, and what it does.

tools.name: start_document
tools.description: Creates a Claim Done case for a document and returns the questions the person needs to answer, with a case_id and access_token for the later steps. Nothing is charged at this step.

tools.name: answer_questions
tools.description: Saves the person's answers (question key => answer) for a case. Returns any questions still open and, for eligible ordinary documents, ready_for_protected_draft when the real protected draft can be created for $0 before payment.

tools.name: prepare_protected_draft
tools.description: For an eligible ordinary document whose questions are complete, starts the real draft for $0 and returns the private dashboard link. tools.name: get_payment_link
tools.description: Returns a hosted Stripe Checkout URL at the live flat price. For an eligible ordinary document, the protected draft must already be ready and the person must have accepted the private review; payment then unlocks the clean PDF, download and delivery options. tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Whether the case is paid, whether a protected draft is processing or ready, whether the person accepted the review, and the private dashboard link. It never returns raw unpaid document text.

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: After genuine payment only: the full text of each drafted document, plus the dashboard link where the person approves it (and, for eligible letters, has it sent). Before payment, protected drafts remain watermarked raster pages on the private dashboard and raw text is never returned.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "start_document" references sensitive artifacts (access_token). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_payment_link, get_status · Private data: list_services, match_problem, start_document, answer_questions, prepare_protected_draft, get_payment_link, get_status, get_document · Public sink: prepare_protected_draft.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_payment_link, get_status · Private data: list_services, match_problem, start_document, answer_questions, prepare_protected_draft, get_payment_link, get_status, get_document · Public sink: prepare_protected_draft

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "answer_questions" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Saves the person's answers (question key => answer) for a case. Returns any questions still open, any follow-up questions the drafting needs, and ready_to_pay when the document can be drafted." → after: "Saves the person's answers (question key => answer) for a case. Returns any questions still open and, for eligible ordinary documents, ready_for_protected_draft when the real protected draft can be created for $0 before payment."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
